response.sql: WITH type_totals AS (SELECT m.Name AS name, CAST(SUM(t.Bytes) AS REAL) / SUM(t.Milliseconds) AS rate, COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track t INNER JOIN MediaType m ON m.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId GROUP BY m.Name), mean_rate AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS mean_rate FROM type_totals) SELECT tt.name, tt.rate, tt.track_count, tt.rate - mr.mean_rate AS rate_minus_mean FROM type_totals tt CROSS JOIN mean_rate mr WHERE tt.rate > mr.mean_rate;

assumptions.assumption: Media types are identified by their Name, so tracks are grouped by MediaType.Name and each name counts once in the mean. The schema does not enforce unique names, but the data is assumed to have none duplicated.
The inner join drops tracks whose MediaTypeId has no matching MediaType row, as the request asks.

Bytes and Milliseconds are integers, so the division casts the byte sum to REAL to avoid integer truncation (SQLite-style semantics). A zero Milliseconds total would make a rate undefined; this query does not guard against it.
A NULL Bytes value adds nothing to the byte total, while that track's Milliseconds and count still apply.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat each media type as identified by its MediaTypeId rather than its name, so two types that share a name would stay separate in the grouping and in the mean.
alternatives.sql: WITH type_totals AS (SELECT m.MediaTypeId AS media_type_id, m.Name AS name, CAST(SUM(t.Bytes) AS REAL) / SUM(t.Milliseconds) AS rate, COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track t INNER JOIN MediaType m ON m.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name), mean_rate AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS mean_rate FROM type_totals) SELECT tt.name, tt.rate, tt.track_count, tt.rate - mr.mean_rate AS rate_minus_mean FROM type_totals tt CROSS JOIN mean_rate mr WHERE tt.rate > mr.mean_rate;
